name: Glossary
blurb: The vocabulary, in plain sentences. Principles, craft, process and the technical terms that show up in delivery specs.

entries.name: Alpha channel
entries.note: The transparency information carried alongside colour.

entries.name: Animatic
entries.note: The storyboard cut to timing, usually with scratch audio. The first honest look at pace.

entries.name: Anticipation
entries.note: A small move opposite to the main action, so the eye is ready for it.

entries.name: Appeal
entries.note: Whether the thing is pleasant to look at. Vague, unfashionable, and real.

entries.name: Arcs
entries.note: Natural movement travels on curves, not straight lines.

entries.name: Aspect ratio
entries.note: The frame's proportions. 16:9, 1:1, 9:16: plan for all three from the start.

entries.name: Bit depth
entries.note: How many values each colour channel can hold. 8-bit banding is the usual symptom.

entries.name: Boardomatic
entries.note: An animatic built straight from boards, before any animation exists.

entries.name: Cel animation
entries.note: Frame-by-frame drawing, named for the transparent celluloid sheets it used to need.

entries.name: Codec
entries.note: How the video is compressed. ProRes to edit, H.264 to deliver, rarely both.

entries.name: Colour space
entries.note: The defined range of colour a file describes: sRGB, Rec.709, and the source of most mismatches.

entries.name: Compositing
entries.note: Combining separate rendered elements into one convincing image.

entries.name: Dithering
entries.note: Trading colour depth for texture with a pattern of pixels. The club's house look.

entries.name: Easing
entries.note: The curve that describes acceleration in and out of a move. Linear reads as mechanical.

entries.name: Exaggeration
entries.note: Pushing past the literal to make the read clearer, not merely louder.

entries.name: Expression
entries.note: A small script driving a property, so motion is computed rather than keyframed.

entries.name: Follow-through
entries.note: Parts of an object that keep moving after the main mass stops.

entries.name: Frame rate
entries.note: Frames per second. 24 for film feel, 25 or 30 for broadcast, 60 for interfaces.

entries.name: Graph editor
entries.note: Where you edit the speed and value curves directly, rather than guessing at handles.

entries.name: Hold
entries.note: A keyframe with no interpolation: the value jumps. The basis of frame-by-frame in a keyframed tool.

entries.name: Interpolation
entries.note: How the software fills the frames between keyframes: linear, bezier, hold.

entries.name: Keyframe
entries.note: A recorded value at a point in time. Everything between them is interpolated.

entries.name: Loop
entries.note: An animation whose last frame flows into its first. Seamlessness is a timing problem.

entries.name: Lottie
entries.note: A JSON format that carries vector animation into apps and the web at any size.

entries.name: Matte
entries.note: A layer used to define what is visible in another layer.

entries.name: Motion tracking
entries.note: Extracting movement from footage so new elements can be attached to it.

entries.name: Null object
entries.note: An invisible layer that exists only to be parented to and animated.

entries.name: Onion skinning
entries.note: Seeing neighbouring frames faintly, so you can draw or place against them.

entries.name: Overlap
entries.note: Different parts arriving at different times, instead of everything landing on one frame.

entries.name: Parenting
entries.note: Attaching one layer's transform to another so it inherits the movement.

entries.name: Pitch deck
entries.note: The document that sells the direction. Often the actual deliverable of week one.

entries.name: Precomp
entries.note: A composition nested inside another. The main tool for keeping a project sane.

entries.name: Procedural
entries.note: Motion generated by rules and parameters rather than by hand-set keyframes.

entries.name: Render
entries.note: Turning the project into frames. Also the thing that always takes longer than the estimate.

entries.name: Resolution
entries.note: Pixel dimensions of the frame. Not the same thing as quality.

entries.name: Rigging
entries.note: Building controls onto artwork so it can be posed and animated without redrawing.

entries.name: Rotoscoping
entries.note: Tracing or masking footage frame by frame to isolate part of it.

entries.name: Secondary action
entries.note: A supporting move that enriches the main one without competing with it.

entries.name: Spacing
entries.note: How far a thing moves between frames. Timing says how long, spacing says how fast it feels.

entries.name: Squash and stretch
entries.note: Deforming a shape to sell weight and impact while preserving volume.

entries.name: Staging
entries.note: Composing the frame so the audience looks at the one thing that matters.

entries.name: Storyboard
entries.note: The shot-by-shot plan. Cheaper to fix here than anywhere downstream.

entries.name: Styleframe
entries.note: A single still that establishes the look of a sequence before anything moves.

entries.name: Timing
entries.note: How long an action takes. The single biggest lever on how something feels.

entries.name: Track matte
entries.note: Using one layer's alpha or luminance to cut out another.

entries.name: Weight
entries.note: The impression of mass, communicated almost entirely through timing and easing.
